highlights.title: Greptile takes bug detection beyond code review with GPT-6 Astra
highlights.summary: How Greptile uses GPT-6 Astra to test user workflows, Daybreak to strengthen security, and Codex to reduce rework.
body: Greptile ⁠ (opens in a new window) builds AI agents that review and test code changes with full context of the codebase. “We are in the business of reducing bugs and making the world’s software more reliable,” says Co-founder and CEO Daksh Gupta.
For Daksh, that mission requires testing an application’s behavior as well as reading its code, and GPT‑6 Astra’s computer use gives Greptile a way to automate testing at scale.

Validating a pull request involves checking whether the code is logically correct, does what the developer intended, is secure, and avoids breaking existing functionality. For some of that testing, you need to actually run the application because reading the code alone might not reveal the problem.

Daksh gives the example of a button that disappears when a website is viewed on an iPhone. With GPT‑6 Astra, Greptile can start a development server for a pull request, resize the browser to an iPhone-sized viewport, and simulate a user moving through the application. The model’s visual understanding lets it inspect the screen and spot the hidden button.

While cash and trade goods do carry over, quest-related items do not. Forts also need to be re-taken, as NG+ resets the map's fog of war.

The NG+ mode has a new exclusive currency - Escudos - earned by completing challenges and looting previously unlocked chests. The currency can be spent on NG+ exclusive outfits and items, and you'll be able to exchange Reales for Escudos at the General Store, too.

Naturally, the game difficulty increases with each NG+ run. Elite soldiers, for instance, will appear more often, and max rank ships will be a more common sight across the water. You can enter NG+ up to five times, with each further runthrough increasing the challenge.

highlights.title: We, the Hated review – standing up to be abused: behind the scenes with Just Stop Oil
highlights.summary: The levels of violence aimed at these protesters is depressing, but their aim is to save the planet: ‘If they want to destroy everything, they’ve got to go through us’ ‘Hated” is not putting it too strongly.
body: ‘H ated” is not putting it too strongly. The strength of feeling against Just Stop Oil, as caught by this documentary, is really disturbing. It’s filmed from inside the climate group’s protests, and as activists block roads, furious drivers hurl abuse. “Have a wash you fucking idiots!” “Middle class wankers!” It gets physical, too – punching, kicking and dragging. One man appears to drive his van at protesters. Another walks along a line of them, pouring water over their heads, one by one.

Film-maker Rich Felgate could not be closer to the action; his girlfriend, Indigo Rumbelow, is an activist. “Don’t look at the camera. I’m a fly on the wall,” he tells her at their shared house, where books about the suffragettes and Gandhi are on the shelves. On the streets, activists glue themselves to roads and fasten their necks together with bike locks. In October 2022, campaigners notoriously lobbed tomato soup at Van Gogh’s Sunflowers. At one road shutdown an angry driver shouts: “You’re children.” But they’re not all young; a vicar in late middle age with Parkinson’s quickly takes his medicine before he’s cuffed.

highlights.title: Anthropic is burning gas to feed the AI boom
highlights.summary: As it prepares to go public, Anthropic's S-1 filing makes generative AI's methane dependency glaringly obvious. "Competition for access to electrical supply and data center locations with adequate power availability is intense." In documents filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission…
body: Anthropic is clear that data centers will run on gas, to the company’s own detriment.

The US, the epicenter for data centers globally, is planning to build more fossil fuel generation capacity than it has in a decade as data centers demand more electricity. Donald Trump’s administration has sought to kill renewable energy projects while tilting the regulatory landscape in favor of fossil fuels, which Trump claims is a more important energy source for powering data centers around the clock than solar and wind farms that generate power intermittently.

Now, a shortage of gas turbines is slowing data center construction. Some developers are installing gas engines on-site as a way to avoid long wait times to connect to power grids. Developers are also turning to more simple turbine technology at these sites as they face backlogs from turbine manufacturers, making on-site power generation less efficient and more polluting as a result.

highlights.title: 9 Spooky 'Far Side' Comics That Are Perfect to Read Before Halloween
highlights.summary: During this time of year, all the classic monsters enjoy their annual resurgence. Vampires rise from their coffins, mummies emerge from their tombs, and witches fly in on their brooms to stalk the world of the living via decorations and costumes.
body: From vampire cows to witches getting cosmetic surgery, these panels feature those famous monsters presented through cartoonist Gary Larson’s famously twisted lens. While he didn’t reserve these comic strips to the spooky season during their original publication, Halloween is still the best time to experience Larson’s wild take on these horror classics.

Since this is Gary Larson we’re talking about here, it only makes sense to kick things off with a cow. Larson once explained his love for cows in a curious way. ''I've always thought the word cow was funny, and cows are sort of tragic figures,” he said. “Cows blur the line between tragedy and humor.'' This is why so many of his comic strips starred the gentle creatures. Over the years, his comics featured dinosaur cows and cannibal cows who eat hamburgers, so it’s only natural that vampire cows would appear too. And since vampires are famously killed by a stake to the heart, so too would Gary Larson’s vampcow be taken down by a steak.

highlights.title: Why Anthropic’s IPO Prospectus Is Missing So Many Key Figures
highlights.summary: Anthropic’s S-1 filing is hundreds of pages long—and it leaves out quite a few financial details. “Anthropic owes investors more information,” one analyst tells WIRED.
body: Anthropic filed its hotly anticipated IPO prospectus on Monday, spelling out parts of the company’s business, strategy, and risk profile ahead of its public debut. Though the filing, known as an S-1, is several hundred pages long, it has some notable omissions—namely, certain financial figures.

“Claude has experienced the fastest enterprise adoption of any technology in history, as demonstrated by revenue growing from $0 at commercial launch in the first quarter of 2023 to $_____ for the three months ended September 30, 2026,” reads the first of dozens of such examples.

It’s relatively common for companies to redact certain information in their S-1 filings, and Securities and Exchange Commission rules allow for a certain degree of leniency around the practice, particularly when it comes to information considered “confidential.”

highlights.title: 8 Most Entertaining Sci-Fi Books of the 21st Century That Are Impossible to Put Down
highlights.summary: Science fiction writers imagine humanity's future in order to explore our present and past. The best sci-fi is a mix of cautionary tale and social commentary, but books about heady topics like artificial intelligence, alien encounters, and galaxy-spanning wars are often filled with dense…
body: John Scalzi is a master of comedic sci-fi, whether penning zany novels like Starter Villain or the silly short stories that got adapted to episodes of the Netflix anthology series Love, Death & Robots. Fans of Star Trek: Lower Decks should check out his Hugo Award-winning novel Redshirts, which follows a group of new ensigns on a starship where away missions have an appallingly high casualty rate. Things get far weirder when the new crew begins investigating the nature of their ship’s confrontations with aggressive aliens and looking for a way to save their lives.

Very much a journey over destination book, Becky Chambers’ originally self-published debut novel follows Rosemary Harper, a woman from Mars who tries to escape her past by joining the crew of a ship tasked with tunneling wormholes through space. Rosemary learns a lot from the quirky aliens she shares the ship with as they protect each other in this sweet story of found family. The cozy book is a perfect read for fans of Firefly or Farscape.

highlights.title: ‘Tokyo Vice’ Producer, Netflix Executive Urge Changes to Japan’s Production Incentive at MPA Seminar as Government Readies Unified Content Body
highlights.summary: “Tokyo Vice” producer Alex Boden and Netflix production policy director Deb Richards urged changes to Japan’s international production incentive at the Motion Picture Association’s annual seminar at the Tokyo International Film Festival, as the government prepares a new body to bring its scattered…
body: He said the minimum spend, raised to JPY800 million ($5.1 million), shut out independent films and co-productions, since most Japanese films cost between $1.5 million and $3 million. He also called for an automatic approval system in place of panel-based selection, which he said made Japan one of the few territories with a subjective incentive, at a time when projects can take three to five years to come together.

“So how does a producer know that they can count on the Japan incentive in advance? That’s the question, and we need a solution,” Boden said. He pointed to Martin Scorsese’s “Silence,” “Pachinko” and “Shōgun” as Japan-set projects that scouted in the country but shot elsewhere, and argued for building training into the incentive, citing the U.K.’s 0.5% ScreenSkills levy as a model.

“You can have a lower incentive, that’s fine, as long as it’s certain, as long as the criteria are clear,” Richards said during the panel. “And that’s one of the things that for the Japan incentive, the criteria is not clear.” She added that applicants could work out why they were turned down only by looking at who was approved, calling the process “opaque.”

highlights.title: Women: was your autoimmune condition misdiagnosed?
highlights.summary: We want to hear from women with autoimmune conditions who received an incorrect or delayed diagnosis. Hundreds of millions of people – roughly one in ten globally – are affected by autoimmune conditions, diseases in which the immune system attacks the body instead of defending it.
body: Research from Cambridge University and the University of East Anglia found women are 43% more likely than men to receive a psychiatric misdiagnosis, meaning an autoimmune issue is misdiagnosed as a psychiatric problem, and 74% more likely to receive a psychosomatic misdiagnosis, meaning symptoms are considered psychological or stress-induced rather than physical. Women also reported significantly longer periods between the onset of symptoms and receiving a diagnosis – one to two years, compared to less than three months for men.

highlights.title: UK government met 137 businesses over AI datacentres – but no environmental groups
highlights.summary: Investigation finds dozens of ministers and civil servants moved into AI roles as government developed datacentre expansion plans. The UK’s policy on datacentres and AI was developed without any meetings with environmental groups, an investigation has found.
body: The nonprofit organisation Spotlight on Corruption said a “considerable revolving door” shaped the government’s development of “AI growth zones”, a central plank of the former prime minister Keir Starmer’s AI and economic policy, with 38 ministers, senior civil servants and special advisers hired to positions in AI companies between July 2024 and September 2026.
Meanwhile, even as top officials left government for jobs at OpenAI and Anthropic, government departments largely failed to engage meaningfully with stakeholders outside the technology industry.

Kamila Kingstone, a campaign lead at the NGO, said: “The government totally failed at the most senior level to speak to environmental NGOs or community groups when developing its flagship policy on AI datacentres. This is despite the serious environmental implications of its plans.”

Over 12 months, Spotlight on Corruption filed 40 freedom of information requests to 18 government agencies, seeking details of meetings and investment figures relating to the government’s policymaking on the growth zones, covering the period between July 2024 and June 2026.

highlights.title: Major 'Avatar: Seven Havens’ Korra Reveal May Be Hiding the Truth About the Cataclysm
highlights.summary: For more than two centuries, the world of Avatar: Seven Havens has remembered Korra as the Avatar who destroyed everything. Everybody from Ellora to New Ba Sing Se has grown up hearing that story, and episode 7 seemingly gives Pavi (Saheli Khan) and Nisha (Aishu Devan) them proof: They witness…
body: At face value, the evidence looks pretty damning. But the more closely you examine what the vision actually shows, the less straightforward Korra ’s apparent rampage becomes.

She isn’t visibly attacking people. She isn’t leveling buildings. She’s targeting pipes carrying what appears to be spiritual energy through a city that’s already on fire. And a change in her clothing suggests that the vision skips over an unknown amount of time before the destruction begins.
We may finally be seeing what Korra did. That doesn’t mean we understand why she did it.

In “What Lies Beneath,” Pavi, Nisha, and Jae (Major Curda) discover a subterranean industrial facility after they break open a growing chunk of Anomaly crystals. After Geet rubs his head against a random switch, a movie begins playing. (“An old-world mover!”) It features technicians wearing white coats and protective gloves, followed by an older Asami at a ribbon-cutting ceremony. Then we see a large building that bears the Future Industries logo, linking the project to the company she inherited from her father.
points: For more than two centuries, the world of Avatar: Seven Havens has remembered Korra as the Avatar who destroyed everything.
Everybody from Ellora to New Ba Sing Se has grown up hearing that story, and episode 7 seemingly gives Pavi (Saheli Khan) and Nisha (Aishu Devan) them proof: They witness…

highlights.title: ‘The view from the Mournes was CS Lewis’s idea of Narnia’: how Northern Ireland inspired a magical kingdom
highlights.summary: Ahead of Netflix’s Chronicles of Narnia dropping early next year, we discover the fantastical landscapes that fired the Belfast-born author’s imagination. On the gable walls of the tough, working-class streets of east Belfast, the mystical beasts of Narnia vie for brick space with balaclava-wearing…
body: Lewis was born in Dundela in 1898 in an attractive terrace house that has sadly since been demolished to be replaced by rather unattractive flats. But elsewhere in this part of the city, the Lewis connection is being built on and celebrated. CS Lewis Square is in the Holywood Arches neighbourhood and has a short walking trail featuring metal sculptures of Mr and Mrs Beaver, Mr Tumnus and other beloved characters from The Chronicles of Narnia. The centrepiece is a gigantic Aslan, towering over all from atop a circular mound.

About 15 minutes’ walk away, St Mark’s church on the Holywood Road is the proud custodian of a much smaller lion that may have inspired Lewis’s creation of Aslan. His grandfather, the Rev Thomas Hamilton, ministered here, living in the rectory for 13 years, and his front door was decorated with a beautiful brass lion’s head doorknob. The original has been removed for safekeeping, but an exact replica attracts thousands of Lewis pilgrims each year.

body: Each year, Climate Week NYC brings together more than 100,000 people in more than 1,000 events across the city to discuss climate challenges, explore solutions, and spur action. Participants come from industry, academia, philanthropy, nonprofits, government, and finance and venture capital. And this year, the mix included a strong, cross-campus presence from MIT.

“The MIT Climate Project is a whole-of-MIT mobilization, but no single institution can deliver the climate solutions the world needs — from reducing greenhouse gas emissions to adapting to a changing climate and building more-resilient communities and systems,” said Wang, who is also the Ford Professor of Engineering in the Department of Mechanical Engineering. “Climate Week New York is important because it convenes the range of stakeholders and sectors that must work together to confront these challenges. When we connect the MIT community with this global network, we uncover powerful possibilities to strengthen not only our own efforts, but the world’s capacity for change.”

highlights.title: Four takeaways from Anthropic’s potentially record-breaking stock market filing
highlights.summary: The AI company’s first public financial disclosures reveal explosive growth, huge costs and risks ranging from cyber-attacks to the limits of safeguards. Anthropic has filed to go public on the US stock market, revealing for the first time the AI research lab’s financials and all the risks – more…
body: The company’s investor prospectus, released Monday, veers from hyperbolic predictions about AI’s “incredible potential” to existential risks of the technology to the reality of its current business: explosive but incredibly expensive growth. The filing to US financial regulators, known as an S-1, provides the public’s first look at an audited version of Anthropic’s finances.

Here’s what you need to know: Anthropic is making a lot of money. It’s also losing a lot of it. The five-year-old firm has been valued between $1.5 and $2tn by some investors but did not list a target valuation in its S-1. Founded in 2021, the company has seen explosive growth every year of its existence.

Anthropic brought in $16.3bn in revenue and lost $80 bn in just the first half of 2026, though much of that was due to a $72.4bn one-off charge. In 2025, the company brought in $4.585bn and lost roughly $33.9bn, per the filing.

Securing computing power accounts for the vast majority of Anthropic’s costs. The company spent nearly $9bn on AI infrastructure in the first half of this year, up from $2.3bn in the same period last year.
points: The AI company’s first public financial disclosures reveal explosive growth, huge costs and risks ranging from cyber-attacks to the limits of safeguards.

highlights.summary: The England captain spoke movingly on night of deserving winners and unintentional hilarity in London. Well, there’s something new. Football: now available in new, genuinely heartwarming flavour.
body: There was a lovely moment at London’s Palladium theatre, with the clock creeping towards 11pm at the end of a startlingly shrill and bloated evening of never-ending awards and never ending award-related excitement.

Not just for Harry Kane, who is now the 2026 men’s Ballon d’Or winner, and in the process placed indelibly in that lineage of elite footballers. But also, frankly, for anyone watching, as Kane stood on stage gazing a little shyly at his golden orb, and kicked off his speech by thanking everyone, paying tribute to everyone, everywhere, then finally cracking into tears and a strangled croak as he thanked his parents for sacrifices made, his wife for always being there, and even, in slightly jarring vibe-shift from the warm honeyed tone, José Mourinho.
Even Kane’s biggest advocates will rarely claim their man is one of a kind, sui generis, in the mode of the Ronaldo-Messi godhead. But Kane is exactly this in his own admirably humble way.

body: “God, you can do anything you want to me; just please make me famous,” Perry freely admits to praying in his youth. (He got “Friends” shortly afterward, but ruefully notes that “God didn’t forget” about the first part.) “The One About Matthew Perry” is more a collation of established facts about Perry’s battles, including a sepsis-induced coma in 2018 resulting from his use of opiates, and an unveiling of new ones. What the project adds are personal testimonies about witnessing said battles up close, plus memorable observations like “intimacy was his greatest fear and his greatest wish.” Though the most memorable lines — “Reality is an acquired taste,” say — fittingly belong to Perry.

highlights.title: The pest I’ll never forget: the rats stood six or seven deep on the lawn beside my dormitory
highlights.summary: All it took was one or two careless teenage girls giving the vermin a taste of their snacks and they became the most well-fed animals imaginable. I’ve written a fair amount about my boarding school years in Nigeria in the 90s, but never about the rats that accompanied my school experience.
body: I will never forget the sight of rats – six or seven deep – congregating at dusk on the scraggly lawn next to my dormitory, like an illegal gathering of political dissidents. They were large (what with their rich diet), thick tails twitching, noses pushed together, damn near whispering. At first, they would scatter when humans approached. Then we had to clap and stomp to get them to shift. Like the proletariat, the rats began to understand their power, and stand their ground. They were no longer pests but now a sort of predator. If this sounds like the beginning of a highbrow horror, that’s how it felt.

These rats were of course in their own habitat, perfectly at home, and adapting to our unwelcome presence. We were the interlopers, with our classrooms and dormitories, and daily assemblies and annual sports days. I can now recognise that dealing with a certain kind of pest is a fact of life in places where nature has not yet been completely decimated. The rats were the price of a kind of freedom. But years later, post-pandemic lockdown, when the rats attempted to colonise New York, I had searing flashes of the rats of my childhood. Yup, still traumatising.
points: All it took was one or two careless teenage girls giving the vermin a taste of their snacks and they became the most well-fed animals imaginable.

body: The STAR 50 Index, which tracks technology and innovation companies on the Shanghai stock exchange, has plunged 40% since June. Other indexes of major companies dropped by about 20% over the same time period.
The precipitous drop has wiped out $2.4tn from the Chinese stock market since May, according to Bloomberg.
AI stocks account for over 40% of the stock market value in China and Hong Kong, according to Goldman Sachs, meaning that any dent in value will send shockwaves across the whole domestic market.

The fall suggests that despite the government’s best efforts to boost China’s technology industries, particularly those which harness the power of AI, the domestic economy does not have the power to sustain a booming market.

highlights.title: ‘The wind goes in all directions’: Fleetwood prepare wet welcome for Arsenal at Highbury
highlights.summary: The Premier League champions may have bigger fish to fry but can expect a feisty reception from League Two strugglers in the Carabao Cup. The headlines around Fleetwood Town are rarely about what happens on the pitch.
body: It is no different this week, although this time football is taking centre stage as Arsenal head to Highbury Stadium on Tuesday for a Carabao Cup fourth-round tie against the League Two side. There is no link to the Gunners’ former home in Islington and the ground is a world away from what the visitors are used to, its capacity a fraction of the Emirates Stadium. The Championship side Sheffield United were deservedly beaten there in the previous round, unable to cope with their opponents or the conditions, but the Cod Army anticipate a sterner test from Mikel Arteta’s aristocrats.

Even against the Blades, the ground was less than half full but Tuesday will bring the venue’s biggest football attendance; the only other time it has sold out was for a fireworks display. The capacity is 5,300 and the stadium has four parking spaces, leaving Arsenal representatives to find alternatives on the street.

Fleetwood have a loyal local fanbase and occasions such as this can aid growth. Since the draw they have sold about an extra 200 season tickets to supporters keen to guarantee a place at the best show in town.

highlights.summary: Quick, simple finger food that children will love for Halloween: pumpkin and carrot fritters with a chilli-coriander relish, and pumpkin baked into a dark chocolate slice. It would be lazy to write, with a rueful shake of the head, that Halloween gets bigger every year. Halloween is huge.
body: Delightfully crisp, rich in flavour and delicately spiced, these are simple to throw together but look and taste spectacular, especially with the zippy relish for dipping.
Coarsely grate the pumpkin and carrot, then wrap them in a clean tea towel or kitchen paper, and squeeze hard to push out any excess moisture.

Put a frying pan on a medium heat, add the oil and spring onions, and cook, stirring, for two to three minutes. Grind the coriander and cumin seeds in a mortar, then add to the pan with the cinnamon and a few generous pinches of salt, and cook for a few minutes more. Add the garlic and ginger, and cook, stirring all the time, for a couple of more minutes. By now, the onions will have softened and the mixture will be smelling irresistibly fragrant. Tip the lot into a large bowl, then add the grated pumpkin and carrots, and the gram flour. Season with a little more salt and plenty of black pepper, then mix to combine.

videos.title: GRIZZLIES at JAZZ | FULL GAME HIGHLIGHTS | October 26, 2026
videos.summary: The Grizzlies defeated the Jazz, 110-105 tonight in Utah. Cedric Coward finished with a team-high 16 points along with 11 rebounds and 4 three pointers for the Grizzlies, while Ty Jerome tallied 15 points, 8 assists in the game. Keyonte George recorded 26 points, 6 assists and 3 rebounds.
body: Never miss a moment with the latest news, trending stories and highlights to bring you closer to your favorite players and teams.
points: The Grizzlies defeated the Jazz, 110-105 tonight in Utah.
Cedric Coward finished with a team-high 16 points along with 11 rebounds and 4 three pointers for the Grizzlies, while Ty Jerome tallied 15 points, 8 assists in the game.

The Grizzlies improve their record to 4-0 with the win, while the Jazz fall to 1-3 for the season.

videos.title: GPT-6.1 Terra is now in orbit
videos.summary: GPT-6.1 Terra: delivering fast and capable computer use at a lower price.
body: GPT-6.1 Terra understands what’s on screen, takes action across apps, writes naturally, and is a more capable model for your whole workday with the efficiency to take on more of it.
GPT-6.1 Terra continues to advance the cost-intelligence frontier across our model families and is a significant step up over GPT‑5.6 Terra, with 50% lower standard API prices.
In ChatGPT Work and Codex, your usage allowance goes further with GPT‑6.1 Terra than with GPT‑5.6 Terra—and far more than with GPT‑6.1 Sol or GPT‑6 Astra.
